mutants.description: Episode start lets the latch causes (inferred OVP and latch_assert) bypass the capture gate, on the belief that a latch trip always marks an episode, while the accumulator still gates them, so the two blocks disagree once the converter has stopped
mutants.reason: After a latch trip has stopped the converter and the host has read and cleared the record, the latch stays set until reset. episode_start is then true on every clock with fault_reg empty, so fault_time keeps following timestamp_ms while fault_reg reads zero. In the original, fault_time stays 0.

mutants.description: fault_time is cleared by a host read only when the record is non-empty, on the belief that an empty record has no start time to clear
mutants.reason: Suppose a host read lands on the same clock as the first cause of an episode (fault_reg empty, episode_start high). fault_reg is cleared, but fault_time latches the timestamp instead of clearing. If that cause was a one-clock transient, such as a single window_trip clock, the host then sees a non-zero fault_time with an empty fault_reg.

mutants.description: The episode start time is latched from the two low bytes of timestamp_ms only, as if the counter were 16 bits wide, so the top byte of fault_time is always zero
mutants.reason: For any episode that begins once timestamp_ms has passed 65535 ms (about 65.5 s after reset), fault_time's upper byte, read through FTIME_2, is 0 instead of timestamp_ms[23:16].
